record.paper_title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
record.original_question: Given a compact 4-manifold presented only by its 0-, 1-, and 2-handles and a gem of that compact manifold, can one construct a gem of the associated closed 4-manifold even when the original gem contains no ρ_3-pair or ρ_4-pair? More specifically, can one recognize the boundary connected sum #_m(S^1 × S^2) combinatorially and, in useful special cases, find sequences of combinatorial moves that create the ρ_3-pairs needed to pass to a gem of the closed manifold obtained by attaching the 3- and 4-handles?

evidence.quote: Another possible improvement would be to study how to obtain a gem of a closed 4-manifold, starting from a gem of the compact one consisting only of handles up to index two, even if no ρ_3- or ρ_4-pair appears in the latter (as assumed in Proposition 9). The problem is obviously a difficult one, since it involves the combinatorial recognition of #m(S1 ×S2) (m > 0) in 3-dimensional topology, but in specific situations it could possibly be faced, for example by detecting sequences of combinatorial moves yielding the desired ρ_3-pairs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A gem (graph-encoded manifold) of dimension n is a regular (n+1)-edge-colored multigraph (Γ, γ) with γ : E(Γ) → {0,1,…,n} such that the topological space obtained by gluing one n-simplex per vertex according to the coloring is a PL n-manifold. Gems represent both closed and compact PL manifolds; in the compact case, the boundary is encoded by the subgraph of "boundary" structure determined by the colors.

For an n-colored gem (Γ, γ) and two distinct colors i, j ∈ {0,…,n}, a ρ_h-pair (h ∈ {2,3,…}) is a pair of i-colored edges joining the same two vertices such that exactly h connected components of the subgraph Γ_{{i,j}} (induced by edges of colors i and j) are involved; equivalently, ρ_h-pairs are local combinatorial configurations whose elimination corresponds to canceling complementary handles in the represented manifold. In dimension 4, ρ_3- and ρ_4-pairs are the moves that allow one to pass from a gem of a compact 4-manifold M (built from 0-, 1-, and 2-handles only) to a gem of the closed 4-manifold M̂ obtained by attaching 3- and 4-handles, provided such pairs are present.

Problem. Let M be a compact PL 4-manifold whose handle decomposition consists only of 0-, 1-, and 2-handles, and assume that ∂M is homeomorphic to the connected sum #_m(S^1 × S^2) for some m ≥ 0, so that there is a (unique up to diffeomorphism) closed PL 4-manifold M̂ obtained from M by attaching 3- and 4-handles. Suppose (Γ, γ) is a 5-colored gem representing M that contains no ρ_3-pair and no ρ_4-pair.

(a) Provide a combinatorial procedure on (Γ, γ), depending only on the colored graph, that recognizes whether the boundary subgraph encodes #_m(S^1 × S^2).

(b) When such recognition succeeds, exhibit an explicit finite sequence of combinatorial moves on (Γ, γ) (within the class of gems representing M) that produces a gem (Γ′, γ′) of M containing at least one ρ_3-pair, so that iterating the procedure yields a gem of the closed 4-manifold M̂.

Solve the problem in general, or, failing that, identify nontrivial families of compact 4-manifolds M (for example, those given by Kirby diagrams of bounded complexity, or with specific 2-handle attaching link types) for which (a) and (b) admit explicit solutions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open direction in the gem-theoretic study of PL 4-manifolds. Recent works (2024–2025) on gem-induced trisections and trisection genus via gem theory continue to use the assumption that ρ_3-/ρ_4-pairs are available to pass from a compact gem to a closed-manifold gem; no construction has been published that handles the general case without such pairs. The underlying difficulty is the combinatorial recognition of #_m(S^1×S^2), which remains a hard 3-dimensional problem.

status_evidence.title: Estimating trisection genus via gem theory
status_evidence.snippet: Gem-induced trisections of compact PL 4-manifolds and applications to trisection genus, using ρ-pair structures.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work continues to depend on ρ-pair availability when relating compact and closed gem representations.

status_evidence.title: Gem-induced trisections of compact PL 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: If the boundary is homeomorphic to a connected sum of sphere bundles over S^1, gem-induced trisections naturally give rise to trisections of the corresponding closed 4-manifold.
status_evidence.claim: The passage to the closed manifold relies on detecting #_m(S^1 × S^2) and on ρ-pair moves, illustrating that the case without ρ_3-/ρ_4-pairs is not generally resolved.
